#2796. Guardians Urged to Sign Ex-Tigers Starting Pitcher

BOSTON, MASSACHUSETTS - APRIL 17: Casey Mize #12 of the Detroit Tigers pitches against the Boston Red Sox during the first inning at Fenway Park on April 17, 2026 in Boston, Massachusetts. (Photo by Brian Fluharty/Getty Images) Getty

CLEVELAND, OHIO - OCTOBER 03: Parker Messick #77 of the Cleveland Guardians reacts after pitching against the Chicago White Sox during the first inning in game one of the American League Division Series at Progressive Field on October 03, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) Getty

The Cleveland Guardians made it to Game 6 of the ALCS before falling to the Tampa Bay Rays.

That sets up a key offseason, with a chance to make the right moves and get to the World Series, and that could involve changing their starting pitching rotation.

The Guardians are known for their pitching, and they'll still have a good core group back.

Foster Griffin, though, seems likely to leave in free agency after his midseason arrival from the Nationals, and so there might be at least one opening.

One MLB insider has a plan for the Guardians to fill that role.

GettyBOSTON, MASSACHUSETTS – APRIL 17: Casey Mize #12 of the Detroit Tigers pitches against the Boston Red Sox during the first inning at Fenway Park on April 17, 2026 in Boston, Massachusetts. (Photo by Brian Fluharty/Getty Images)

ESPN's Jeff Passan wrote a new article on Wednesday in which he put on the table the idea of the Guardians signing Casey Mize.

Mize was formerly a No. 1 overall pick by the Detroit Tigers out of Auburn. He remained with the Tigers until the 2026 trade deadline, when they shipped him to the San Diego Padres.

Now, Mize is a free agent and could potentially fit the Guardians' roster.

"While the Guardians' aggressiveness at the trade deadline helped them reach the ALCS, nobody expects them to replicate that in free agency," Passan writes. "With the emergence of Chase DeLauter and trade for Jo Adell, their outfield is set for the first time in years. Their infield is solid, too, with the exception of first base, and between that and designated hitter, Cleveland should be in on midtier power bats. What the Guardians really could use is one more solid starting pitcher, preferably on a shorter-term deal, with real upside. And the ideal candidate is right there for them."

Mize struggled with the Padres, but he's got a solid track record, and Cleveland sure knows how to get the most out of its pitchers.

GettyCLEVELAND, OHIO – OCTOBER 03: Parker Messick #77 of the Cleveland Guardians reacts after pitching against the Chicago White Sox during the first inning in game one of the American League Division Series at Progressive Field on October 03, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images)

If the Guardians added Mize, they'd have a full pitching rotation.

They've already got Parker Messick and Gavin Williams established at the front of the group.

Tanner Bibee and Joey Cantillo will both be back for the 2027 season, too.

With Mize, Cleveland would have a logical five-man staff to begin the new campaign and chase a World Series.

#2792. Max Verstappen questions Ferrari’s decision to let Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc race freely

Following his impressive win at Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez, Max Verstappen said he would never put two number one drivers together if he were a team principal of Ferrari. He believes the battle between Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc gifted him the win in Mexico.

The Ferrari pair fought hard on the opening lap at the Mexico City Grand Prix, and Verstappen took advantage of the clash, winning the race, with Hamilton second and Leclerc fourth after a time penalty.

Asked about it by Viaplay during the Sao Paulo Grand Prix weekend, the Dutchman said the situation could have been avoided.

"I've said it before, and a lot of people often don't agree, but if I was a team principal, I'd never get two number one drivers because then you get things like this," he said.

"One won't yield for the other because they both think they can win, and that's how I am too. And if I was a team principal, I'd change this."

He added that Ferrari would have been better served with a clear pecking order.

"If you had a clear number one and number two, they would've gone through the first corner as P1 and P2 and finished like that. Or P1 and P3, that's fine too, because as a team you're still scoring great points."

Ferrari has consistently confirmed that both drivers are free to race each other. Following what became a dramatic weekend for the Scuderia, team chief Fred Vasseur held a meeting with his two drivers. He confirmed to the media that during this, they had "squashed it".

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari

Ferrari came away from Interlagos with just six points, as Leclerc and Hamilton finished eighth and ninth. The team is still second in the standings, 95 points ahead of Red Bull, with three races left.

Speaking at the circuit, Vasseur said: "We did [the meeting] yesterday evening because I had to fly back to Europe between the two races, but it went well.

"It was good to discuss, good to clarify my position and their position. It was good to do and now we turn the page and we are focused on the next one.

"The guidelines is still the same. They accumulated perhaps a bit of frustration because they are starting each weekend side-by-side and you have a kind of accumulation of fact. But at the end of the day, the guidelines is always the same.

"They need to respect each other, they are two competitors with the fighting spirit for sure, but they need to have respect for the other one, but mainly and firstly, they need to respect the brand, the team, the people working at home, the people working on track. I think we are putting a lot of effort on this, and the message was clear and will stay clear."

#2779. Celtics will be without star player vs Toronto Raptors

TORONTO — The Celtics and Raptors will each miss key players as they meet on Wednesday night.

For the Celtics, Paul George is out with an illness; the star is just a day removed from a 36-point performance against his former squad, the Philadelphia 76ers. Everyone else on the Celtics will play on the second night of a road back-to-back; the team flew from Philadelphia to Toronto late Tuesday night, and Mitchell Robinson and Jayson Tatum, both of whom have gotten one rest game this season, are among them.

George has been the Celtics' second-leading scorer so far this season; he's averaging 22 points, 5.2 rebounds, 3.8 assists, and 2.1 steals per game. He's also been the team's most efficient scorer, shooting 48.8% from the field and 44% from three. The Celtics are 0-1 without him so far this season; they lost by 16 to the Houston Rockets last Monday.

The Raptors could be significantly shorthanded; Scottie Barnes (left groin strain) and Kawhi Leonard (left knee injury management) are both out, while Trayce Jackson-Davis (illness), Colin Murray-Boyles (illness), and Immanuel Quickley (right hamstring injury management) are all questionable.

After blowing out the 76ers on Tuesday night, the Celtics lead the Eastern Conference at 9-2. The Raptors have the 6th-best record in the East at 5-5. The Celtics have won four straight; the Raptors are coming off a loss to the Memphis Grizzlies.

The Celtics are in the middle of their third back-to-back of the season, and Jayson Tatum has played in every single back-to-back game so far.

But last week in Charlotte, he said he's receptive to conversations around his rest management.

"It's my 10th year, so I understand the balance of wanting to play every game, and rest, and back-to-backs, three-in-fours, five-in-sevens," Tatum said. "It's always a conversation. We talk about it. We have a plan. I don't really like sitting out on away games, but we just kind of figure it out as we go."

Tatum said he does not like missing road games, and that has factored into his decision to play on the second nights of multiple back-to-backs this season.

"[That's] part of it, and just kind of the mental aspect of it," he said. "I used to always play back-to-backs, and obviously health is most important, and how I'm feeling physically. But it was an opportunity for me to test myself out, to see how I felt playing the back-to-backs, traveling, getting in at a certain time, and see how I felt after that. I kind of just really wanted to go through that for myself, and I felt really good."

#2775. Tokenization platform Securitize gains 10% postmarket on Q3 results, move into asset-backed finance

Tokenization platform Securitize climbed about 10% postmarket after reporting third quarter growth alongside increased operating expenses, and announcing an expansion into asset-backed finance through a strategic acquisition.

Miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively new corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure. Tokenized assets on the platform grew 9% in the third quarter, to $4.8 billion, from the same period a year ago. Aggregate transaction volume rose 20% from a year ago, to $4.3 billion. Revenue of $11.5 million was up 28% from last year.

The growth came as bullish sentiment around tokenization gained traction throughout the third quarter, ahead of the Security and Exchange Commission formalizing the long awaited Innovation Exemption on Sept. 17, which created a temporary pathway for trading of certain tokenized stocks and strengthened the regulatory outlook.

Profitability is still meaningfully below year-ago levels, due in part to costs associated with going public over the summer, as well as the scaling up of the tokenization business at an active time for the entire sector, Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo told CNBC in an exclusive interview.

Securitize reinforced "certain areas of the company like finance, compliance, legal [and] cybersecurity," which increased corporate costs "compared to a year ago when we were privately held," Domingo said. "We're in in a very good position. The adjusted EBITDA … is improving significantly from previous quarters."

Securitize reported an adjusted EBITDA loss of $2 million, compared with positive adjusted EBITDA of $3.6 million a year ago, better than a $5.5 million loss in the second quarter. The company posted a 183% increase in operating costs and expenses.

Also on Monday, the Securitize board authorized a $50 million share buyback and announced the acquisition of River One, an institutional asset-backed financing platform developing technology to connect stablecoin capital with traditional lending markets. Terms were not disclosed.

Securitize sees an opportunity to modernize the $9 trillion market for asset backed finance by using stablecoins to finance real world assets, generate yield and tokenize investment positions and credit products, Domingo said.The acquisition also marks an expansion beyond Securitize's core niche markets at a time when tokenization's competitive landscape is growing, with traditional asset managers like BlackRock and Franklin Templeton, and established financial market infrastructure providers like DTCC and Broadridge, entering the industry.

"We have been very active in tokenized funds, treasuries [and] yield … And we've been obviously recently very active in tokenized stocks, so this adds another piece of the puzzle in the emerging tokenization space for us to capture revenue growth."

#2771. Jaylen Brown explains apparent snub of former teammate Jayson Tatum: 'I wasn't paying attention'

Two days before playing his former team for the first time since being traded this summer, Philadelphia 76ers star Jaylen Brown told reporters he had "nothing to talk about" with ex-teammate Jayson Tatum.

Apparently he meant it — and it might have had something to do with lamb chops. Figuratively speaking.

Before Tuesday's game at Philadelphia's Xfinity Mobile Arena, Tatum approached Brown and gave him a tap on the arm and a few on the chest. Brown wouldn't even look in the direction of the player with whom he won an NBA championship, made two NBA Finals appearances and played in five Eastern Conference championship series during nine seasons as Celtics teammates.

After the game, a 123-101 Celtics win, Brown implied to reporters that he didn't notice Tatum's attempt to interact with him.

"I'm just focused on coming out and doing what's best for my team," Brown said when asked about the apparent snub. "Everything else was just — to be honest, I wasn't paying attention. But credit to Jayson, he played well tonight. Credit to the Celtics, they executed, they shot the hell out of the ball, and they were the better team tonight."

Read more: Jaylen Brown video sparks furor over how Beverly Hills police treat Black people

Tatum also dismissed the pregame non-encounter as no big deal.

"No headlines about anything like that," Tatum told reporters. "I was just getting ready for the game, ready for jump ball, go out there and compete, have some fun and try to get a win."

Still, things have been a bit frosty between the two players in the aftermath of a July 6 trade that sent Brown to Philadelphia — after spending his first 10 NBA seasons in Boston — in exchange for Paul George, two first-round draft picks and two second-round picks.

Celtics teammates Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown share a laugh during a 2025 game against the New York Knicks in Boston. (Maddie Meyer / Getty Images)

In October, Bleacher Report posted a clip on Instagram of Tatum saying he was "caught off guard" by the trade. Brown responded in the comment section of that post with a blue hat emoji, which is often used to represent the word "cap" when being used as slang for "lie."

Asked about the situation during an Oct. 23 news conference, Tatum insisted "there's no beef" between the two players.

Read more: LeBron James says 'family is safe' after arrest of alleged stalker outside Brentwood home

"I think he's right. There's no beef," Brown told reporters. "Jason comes from a wonderful family. We've accomplished some great things. He's a hell of a basketball player. He's got a great PR team. There's no beef but, you know, it might be a little lamb chops and some gravy, you know what I mean? He should stay ready at all times."

Asked why he would say that, Brown responded: "Just, you know, that's what it is. No beef. It should never ever be that. It's just basketball. We're both blessed, but it might be a little lamb chop. We'll be all right."

Brown was then asked if he had been suggesting that Tatum was being untruthful about the trade situation.

Read more: What we've learned about the first-place Lakers

"Hey, look, like I said, it's no beef," Brown said. "The PR and all that type stuff is it is what it is, but I think we're just both focused on what's in front of us."

George was the leading scorer in Tuesday's game, with 36 points, while Tatum added 21 points, six rebounds and two blocked shots. Brown netted 13 points, his lowest output in 11 games with the 76ers.

"I was looking forward to this," Brown said after the game. "I was looking forward to playing well, but you know, s— happens. You just get ready for the next one, I guess."

#2770. Caio Borralho lists trio of title-shot-worthy contenders, including himself

NEW YORK – Caio Borralho expected to face a higher-ranked opponent than Yousri Belgaroui in his next outing.

While the matchup initially didn't meet the expectations of Borralho (18-2 MMA, 8-1 UFC), he'll get the opportunity to stay active against a new challenge in Belgaroui (11-3 MMA, 3-0 UFC) at Madison Square Garden in the feature bout at middleweight (Paramount+).

For Borralho, No. 7 in the latest USA TODAY Sports/MMA Junkie middleweight rankings, agreeing to take a fight against an unranked opponent initially gave him pause.

"To be honest, in the beginning, I was like, 'It doesn't make sense,'" Borralho told reporters at media day. "Because I was calling Dricus (du Plessis), I was supposed to fight (Joe) Pyfer, and all that. At the end of the day, when I stopped to think about this fight, I was kind of, 'That's the fight.' There's no one else to fight. I've fought most of the guys in the top 15, I won most of them. There was no fight until January, February, so I wanted to stay active."

Borralho is coming off a unanimous decision win over Reinier de Ridder at UFC 326 in March, a successful bounce-back after his first loss in the promotion to Nassourdine Imaov last September. Despite not having a number next to his name, Belgaroui has turned heads in just three UFC appearances. He's stopped each opponent by strikes, which is something Borralho has been studying closely – although there's more to his game.

"I think he's a very good striker for sure," Borallho said. "Everybody knows that. He has all these titles in kickboxing and all that, so he's a very good striker. He knows how to manage distance. He's very tall, and this is something new (for me), but the thing that I notice on him, that he does very good against wrestlers. He knows how to get up really good, how to fight the hands all the time, how to use the cage in his favor. So, I think he has all these good attributes on his game that I need to figure out on Saturday."

With a win over Belgaroui, Borralho believes he would maintain his position among a shortlist of contenders ready for a shot at the middleweight title. With Sean Strickland's next title defense expected against Nassourdine Imaov, Borralho believes it's important to stay active and be ready for any opportunity to earn the next title shot.

"We have three big names right now to go to the belt," Borralho said. "I don't think Khamzat (Chimaev) deserves right now to go to the belt. I think we have Pyfer, Brendan Allen, and myself. I think the three of us are doing a very good run, we are facing the best guys, and any three of us in the mix. ... After my win on Saturday, we might fight each other and see whoever goes first."

Jabari Falls, Colon — Falls helped Colon beat Climax-Scotts on the road Friday in a regional win. He carried the ball 26 times for 181 yards and two scores.

#2765. NBA Week 4 Injury Report: Keyonte George latest early-season injury for Jazz

The Jazz have had terrible injury luck to start the season. Jaren Jackson Jr. should miss about another 4-6 weeks due to an MCL tear. Lauri Markkanen has missed their last two games with a right wrist sprain. Keyonte George missed Tuesday's game with an ankle injury, though both George and Markkanen could end up returning to play on Wednesday. Of course, Jusuf Nurkić still hasn't made his season debut due to a toe injury.

That has left Utah shorthanded early on this year, which has contributed to their 1-10 start. However, especially recently, that has allowed others to thrive. Darryn Peterson has stepped up in a big way lately, with the first three 20-point games of his career coming over Utah's last three games. The hot starts of other rookies have overshadowed Peterson, but if he continues to produce to this level, he'll quickly remind everyone why he was the No. 2 overall pick and will be one of the best rookies in fantasy basketball.

Ace Bailey has also gotten the chance to shine, though not in the way that many expected when he was drafted. He was supposed to just be a shot-creating scorer, but he has done more as a playmaker and as a defender, which has worked out well for fantasy managers. That doesn't mean he can't score, which he proved on Tuesday by scoring a season-high 23 points. Isaiah Collier didn't start in place of George, with Josh Okogie getting the nod instead and Peterson playing point guard. However, Collier was productive off the bench with a 17/5/5 line that included four triples. Even if he's coming off the bench, Collier can continue to be streamed, assuming George remains out.

Thankfully, there aren't too many other injury updates around the league. Hopefully that's a trend that continues.

#2759. With all eyes on the Jays, Paul George lands first blow in renewed Sixers-Celtics rivalry

They say hindsight is 20/20, but was there anything more obvious — or perhaps anything more Sixers — than the night that was supposed to centered around Jaylen Brown vs. Jayson Tatum being dominated by the salary the Sixers sent out to Boston to acquire Brown?

Paul George's 36 points led a Celtics three-point onslaught that allowed them to defeat the Sixers by 22 points in Brown's first game against his old team since the blockbuster trade in the summer. While emotions were running high for a lot of the night's participants, George didn't feel any extra need to make a statement against the team he spent the last two seasons with.

"My job was just to come in and support JT and be the best version that I could be for him," George said after the game. "That was my only focus."

There really doesn't get much better support than going 6-of-11 from three-point range. The Sixers were frustrated with their inability to stop George getting open from behind the arc, especially his former teammates who know him well.

"He played within the game too, that's what Paul does. He plays within the game, he takes what the defense gives him, and we gave him too many open looks tonight," Tyrese Maxey said. "For him to even be able to get up 11 threes, that's the issue. We know what PG does, we shouldn't even been allowing him to get up 11 threes, and that's on us."

Maxey, along with several other Sixers, were happy to reconnect with a teammate they got along with well during his time. The sting of what PG had just done to them on the floor was still on their minds when asked what it was like to see him again though.

"It's good to see Paul," Maxey said. "I didn't want to see Paul get six threes, 30 points. I love him, love his family, I didn't care less, I wanted him to score zero points."

As someone who went through similar injury struggles, Joel Embiid always seemed to have a good relationship with George. He detailed that while in classic Embiid fashion, trolling Tatum a little bit in the process.

"Off the court, we have a special relationship. Families are close, especially both of our kids," Embiid said. "I'm extremely happy for him. You know, he's healthy. He's playing well. He's been … the start of the season, you see what he did tonight. You can kind of say he's been the best player on some level."

George seemed happy to reunite with old teammates as well, referring to them as brothers throughout the night, but his return was never going to elicit the same emotion as lamb chops and gravy. That might have been different if he had been a Sixer longer, but as he told reporters at shoot around before the game, he was only in Philadelphia for two years.

The Sixer crowd didn't give him the same level of venom that's typically gone to star players since departing, James Harden in particular has really heard it from Sixers' crowds each time he's come back. Most of the crowd's animosity was aimed at Tatum, but George still had to deal with some rotten fan behavior. Towards the end of the game, the Sixers called a timeout after another Celtics three and George was seen giving the middle finger towards the crowd.

It turns out that despite being a Celtic, George was pretty justified in that response.

"There was a fan being an asshole. Ball rolled to him, he looked me dead in my eyes, dropped the ball on the ground as if, I'm a dog to go fetch or go get it, instead of passing the ball to me like a normal fan would do," George said, "so then I rolled him a middle finger in return."

Despite all the new exciting parts of this team, a max player coming back to light up the Sixers in his return to South Philadelphia is a story all too familiar.

At least George isn't the type of guy to scream "Jaylen Brown over me??!!" down the tunnel after doing so.

#2755. Matt LaFleur "shocked" Vikings acquired Kirk Cousins for only a third-round pick

Packers head coach Matt LaFleur was Kirk Cousins’ position coach when the quarterback came into the league.

Now the two are set to match up on opposite sidelines again after the Raiders traded Cousins to the Vikings on Tuesday.

LaFleur told reporters in his Wednesday press conference that he’s expecting Cousins to start Sunday’s matchup between Minnesota and Green Bay.

“Yeah, he’ll be out there. He’ll be starting. Fairly confident in that,” LaFleur said. “Obviously, he’s got familiarity with their system. Even if he didn’t, he’s a really intelligent guy and I think he’s been playing at a high level.”

What did make LaFleur raise an eyebrow was the trade compensation, as Minnesota sent a third-round pick to Las Vegas for Cousins.

“I was surprised they didn’t get more for him, quite honestly — I was shocked what they traded him for,” LaFleur said. “It was mind-blowing to me.”

While Cousins played under Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell in 2023 and 2024, LaFleur said what Cousins has been doing with the Raiders this year still has relevance when putting together this week’s game plan.

“You definitely watch some of that, see what he’s had success with, what he’s comfortable with,” LaFleur said. “Obviously, he’s got a long track record with that offense with all those years in Minnesota with Kevin. And [there are still] a lot of the key pieces that were there with him.”

In nine games for the Raiders this year, Cousins completed 64.1 percent of his passes for 2,340 yards with 20 touchdowns and eight interceptions.

#2754. Alexander Ovechkin announces this will be his last NHL season: 'Let's have fun'

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Alex Ovechkin's 22nd NHL season will be his last, the Washington Capitals superstar announced on Monday."This is gonna be my last year," Ovechkin told his teammates in a video the Capitals posted to social media. "It's sad, but it is what it is. We have an unbelievable team this year. There are 82 games left. Let's make the playoffs, and let's have fun."

Ovechkin has already established himself as the greatest goal-scorer in hockey history with 929 tallies, and he still has 82 games to add to that total before he hangs up his skates.

The No. 1 overall pick in the 2004 NHL Draft, Ovechkin immediately established himself as a prolific scorer by notching 52 goals en route to winning the Calder Trophy as a rookie.

Since then, Ovechkin has won the Rocket Richard Trophy as the NHL's leading goal-scorer a record nine times. The Capitals legend's resume also features an Art Ross Trophy and three Hart Trophy wins.

The crowning achievement in Ovechkin's illustrious career is leading Washington to its first Stanley Cup in 2017-18. After coming up short in a number of postseasons prior to that, Ovechkin led all playoff performers with 15 goals and won the Conn Smythe Trophy as a result.

Following the 2025-26 season, there was speculation that Ovechkin could retire, but he signed an incentive-laden one-year deal with the Caps.Sensing that this could be Ovechkin's final season, the Capitals loaded up to give their franchise icon one more shot at the Stanley Cup. Washington signed former Buffalo Sabres winger Alex Tuch in free agency and acquired winger Jordan Kyrou from the St. Louis Blues via trade.

No team is as loaded on the wings as the Capitals, and they have one of the best rosters in the Metro Division. Washington has the ingredients to challenge the defending Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes and get Ovechkin one more ring before he rides off into the sunset.

#2752. Big Mitch quietly showed exactly why the Celtics signed him

Tuesdays' big-stage matchup between the Boston Celtics and Philadelphia 76ers saw no shortage of storylines. Buried beneath the Jaylen Brown vs. Jayson Tatum, Celtics vs. Sixers rivalry, and the battle of the uncs, Mitchell Robinson quietly entered his first real measuring stick game.

What did he have for Boston as they matched up against Joel Embiid (alongside four other massive names)?

Adding Robinson over the summer came with plenty of luxrious hypotheticals. That's all great. More than anything, Boston clearly needed some extra frontcourt help after their previous rotation of Neemias Queta, Nikola Vucevic, and Luka Garza had no answer for post-appendectomy Embiid in the playoffs last spring.

Queta spent much of the series in foul trouble, while neither Vucevic nor Garza was strong enough to keep the former NBA MVP away from the basket. Buckets came easy for The Process and so did the wins.

Embiid dominated the Celtics in Games 5-7 to help lead the Sixers to a 3-1 comeback in what was their first playoff series win over Boston in 44 years.

Big Mitch hasn't quite met the expectations surrounding his arrival just yet. He hasn't been the same nuisance on the offensive glass as he was seemingly everytime he'd play Boston as a member of the New York Knicks. He's looked out of shape. His quickness and defensive playmaking have remained hidden talents.

Plus, the "Sheets FC" analytics nerd portion of the fanbase would tell you that those numbers don't favor Celtics Mitch just yet.

You wouldn't have been able to guess all that if you just watched him for the first time on Tuesday. Robinson clearly understood the assignment.

It's not always easy to notice defense when you watch a game live. Sometimes you're just watching the ball. Others, the fundamental, non-highlight-worthy defense doesn't jump off the screen at you. The experience is a little different when Embiid catches the ball in the post and you get war flashbacks to the spring.

You just kind of expect him to take a few power dribbles and work his was to the rim.

Instead, Robinson consistently held his ground and forced the longtime 76er to work further from the basket. He also remained under control while getting physical — an important skill when guarding one of the league's most profound grifters. Like, Embiid averages more free-throws per game this season than field-goal attempts.

So, the fact that Mitch was able to defend him without fouling (except for when he decided to sloppily closeout on a three-point attempt for some reason, despite Embiid shooting 10% from deep entering the game) was huge.

The Louisiana native guarded the seven-foot-two center on 24.3 partial possessions, held him to five points on 1-3 from the field, and forced a turnover. Embiid couldn't move him. It was like watching him try to back down one of Mitch's monster trucks.

For perspective, Queta guarded Embiid on 18.1 partial possessions in Boston's Game 7 loss to Philly back in May. Embiid scored 14 points on Queta while shooting an efficient 6-11 from the floor.

The Portuguese big man was much better Tuesday, in fairness. Queta limited Embiid to just three points on 17 partial possessions.

Both his play, and Robinson's as his backup, were a clear step in the right direction. There's a lot of season left. Robinson has to continue to uphold a defensive standard. But, if he looks the way he did against Embiid and the 76ers, then Boston will have aptly plugged the hole that sank their ship last spring.

#2750. NFL Injury Report, Week 10: Latest news, updates for Puka Nacua, George Pickens, more players for fantasy football

It's the halfway point of the 2026 NFL season and by now you likely have weathered plenty of injuries on your fantasy football rosters. We have a handful of big names we're tracking going into Week 10 while four teams are on bye — the Bears, Broncos, Buccaneers and Eagles. Below we'll update you on the latest injury news, plus provide some useful fantasy football analysis.

Sam Darnold, SEA (quad/ribs) — Out for Week 10

Drew Lock, SEA (oblique) — Should be good to start

Deshaun Watson, CLE (concussion) — Set to start

Gardner Minshew, ARI (elbow) — On IR with torn UCL

Mahomes: At the time of Mahomes' injury in Week 9, it looked as though we were watching a QB who may be done for the season. But after exiting due to an elbow injury, Mahomes was able to return in the Chiefs' 35-12 win over the Jets on Sunday. Mahomes completed 23-of-31 passes for 242 yards and two scores, posting fewer than 20 fantasy points for the fifth time in the past six games.

Kenneth Walker III continues to be the focal point of the offense as the passing game lacks depth and a vertical threat. The Chiefs face the Falcons in Week 10 and Mahomes was a full practice participant Wednesday, a good sign for him being able to play. If he's able to go, it'll be a chance for him to work with new receiver Josh Downs, who came over in a trade with the Colts on Tuesday.

Seahawks QBs: Head coach Mike Macdonald already went on the radio Monday and said Darnold will be out Week 10 against the Raiders. Lock underwent tests on an oblique injury he suffered Sunday and those came back "good," so he's in line to start again. The Raiders have been a great fantasy matchup for QBs this season, allowing the fifth-most points to the position. However, the Seattle offense has struggled a bit with lack of depth behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Lock is back in the QB2 streaming convo for Sunday and isn't a bad spot start if you have Caleb Williams or Bo Nix on bye.

Minshew: The Cardinals QB is on IR with a torn UCL. That means rookie Carson Beck will start. If you remember back to the preseason, Beck was actually pretty good. There's a chance this is a good move overall for the offense, particularly TE Trey McBride. But Arizona is down WR Michael Wilson (neck) and Beck won't have many other options in the passing game. In Superflex, Beck is worth a speculative add to see how he does in Week 10 against the Rams.

Willis: The Dolphins surprised us before the trade deadline by placing Willis on IR, which could mean he's done for the season this late in the year. He'll miss at least the next four games, which would mean the soonest he could be back is Week 14 against Chicago. 2025 sixth-round pick Kyle McCord is the backup and will start in Week 10 versus the Colts. Brady Cook will be the backup.

Miami's passing offense enters Week 10 ranked 30th in the NFL. Chances are it doesn't get much better with McCord under center, but we'll need to see. It's a downgrade to receivers like Malik Washington, Greg Dulcich and Caleb Douglas in the short term until we assess things. Ollie Gordon II could be leaned on a bit more, and McCord may use the RB and Dulcich as safety valves.

TreVeyon Henderson, NE (illness — ruled out)

Josh Jacobs, GB (finger) — Report: Out a max of three weeks

Travis Etienne Jr., NO (hamstring) — Chance to return this week

Patriots RBs: Stevenson exited Sunday's blowout loss to the Packers early and did not return. Henderson has missed the past two games after being hospitalized due to "unexplained neurological symptoms." Stevenson missed practice Wednesday and will reportedly be sidelined multiple weeks. The Patriots face the Lions in Germany this week, which means Corey Kiner is likely to take over as the lead back. He finished with a solid 8-55-1 rushing line against Green Bay, though most of that production was on a fourth-quarter drive when the game was essentially over. Lan Larison would be the RB2 for New England.

Jacobs: On the other side of that game, Jacobs suffered a fractured finger in the win over the Patriots and didn't return. Rushing duties were then split between Pierre Strong Jr. and Kaleb Johnson with MarShawn Lloyd out. Johnson rushed for 68 yards on 14 carries with a score. He looked pretty good running the ball for a team that has struggled to do so all season. But it was also in a blowout. Even so, Johnson is a proactive add off the waiver wire with Jacobs expected to miss time. Green Bay faces the Vikings in Week 10 before the bye and it would be hard to trust any Packers RB against one of the best defenses in the NFL. Johnson will be a risky flex play against Minnesota in Week 10. Strong isn't a bad add in deeper PPR formats and keep an eye on Lloyd, who could be back soon.

Puka Nacua, LAR (knee/turf toe) — To miss "significant" time

Michael Wilson, ARI (neck) — Out for season

Luther Burden III, CHI (concussion) — on bye

Nacua: Sean McVay told reporters Wednesday that the wideout will avoid IR for now but miss "significant" time with knee sprains and turf toe. The Rams are already without Davante Adams, but McVay did offer hope that the veteran WR could return from a ruptured hamstring as soon as Week 13. For now, there isn't much WR depth. Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell and the trio of tight ends — Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson and Davis Allen — will need to step up. We'd throw Terrance Ferguson into that group, but he remains on IR and isn't expected back in Week 10. L.A. should lean more on its run game with Kyren Williams and Blake Corum.

With Nacua out, it's a downgrade to the passing game and Matthew Stafford's fantasy outlook. It's a slight bump up for Williams and Corum, both of whom are involved in the passing game plenty. The Rams take on the Cardinals before their bye in Week 11, which is an easy draw for the run game. Mumpfield isn't a bad waiver wire add, along with Atwell in deeper formats. But don't expect any receiver to get the type of volume like Nacua did.

Michael Wilson: The WR will miss the rest of the season due to a neck injury. It's a tough blow for managers who were hoping for more following the Marvin Harrison Jr. trade. Instead, Wilson struggled, failing to reach double-digit fantasy points in four of the past five games. With Jalen Brooks and Kendrick Bourne on injured reserve, Arizona is very, very thin at WR.

Simi Fehoko, Reggie Virgil and Devin Duvernay all played significant snaps in Week 9 against Seattle. None of them did much, while Trey McBride was obviously the main target for Gardner Minshew. Though, Minshew is on IR with a torn UCL and the team will start rookie Carson Beck at QB this week.

Pickens: The Cowboys held Pickens out of their win over the Colts in Week 9. As a result, CeeDee Lamb went off for 10-195-1 while third-string WR Ryan Flournoy was quiet with two catches for 53 yards. Dallas leaned on the run game, leading most of the first half. It's clear the offense missed Pickens and will need him ready for a key NFC matchup with the Niners in Week 10. Pickens was a limited practice participant Wednesday. If Pickens is out again, Flournoy remains a flex option, while Lamb would remain a target hog and elite WR1.

#2748. Zac Taylor: Duke Tobin is "really apologetic" after backing out of trade with Eagles

On Tuesday, the Bengals backed out of a trade for edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie after it was revealed that the deal might cost Cincinnati with a future compensatory draft pick.

During his Wednesday press conference, head coach Zac Taylor explained the situation from the perspective of Bengals director of player personnel — and de facto General Manager — Duke Tobin.

“Obviously, we tried something yesterday,” Taylor said. “Duke was very explicit with me when he came and spoke to me about how he wanted this portrayed. I’m not comfortable doing it, but I’m going to do what he asked. We did make an effort to put some depth in there in place of Cashius [Howell]. As we got into it, it was going to be more costly than we initially anticipated.

“He’s really apologetic about it and wants it made clear — Philly was a great trade partner. It was on our end. Certainly, we have a ton of confidence in our front office and how they do things. They’ve given us the players that have allowed us to be 6-2 right now, and playing at such a high level. So, we’ll put that behind us and move forward, and just get excited for this game on Sunday. Our locker room is in a great place right now.”

Taylor noted Tobin didn’t really tell him how everything went down and he didn’t ask the question.

“It doesn’t really matter to me. It probably took three minutes of my day yesterday away from watching tape,” Taylor said. “So, got a lot of faith in how those guys operate and we’ll just move forward with it.”

With that, the Bengals didn’t make any deadline moves to improve the team. Taylor said he and Tobin like where the team is.

“I think you can talk to the players in the locker room, they really like where we’re at,” Taylor said. “So, this is a team with a lot of confidence right now. I know it’s a fun period of time — the weeks leading up to the trade deadline — for fans … but the truth is, we really like where we’re at. Our guys are playing with a high degree of confidence and we’ll continue to move forward.”

#2746. Kevin O'Connell: Too early to commit wholeheartedly to Kirk Cousins starting Sunday

The Vikings traded a third-round pick for Kirk Cousins on Tuesday because they need to improve their quarterback play, but head coach Kevin O’Connell stopped short of saying that Cousins will jump immediately into the lineup this week.

Cousins is familiar with O’Connell’s offense because of his previous stint playing for him with the Vikings and O’Connell said on Wednesday that will help speed up the acclimation process. He added that there are some differences from when Cousins was last with the team in 2023 and that he wants “to be fair to Kirk and make sure he feels good about it,” but that “we acquired Kirk to join a 6-2 football team and play.”

#2745. The Worst Loss in Pelicans History

Winning in the NBA is hard; growing pains are always going to happen, especially with a franchise under a new coach and mentality. But after an embarrassing showing by a short-handed New Orleans Pelicans, more questions arose than answers. There is talent on the roster, but the fit may never be right for the team to be competitive.

With Zion Williamson and Trey Murphy III out, the second game of a back-to-back on the road against Steph Curry, arguably the best shooter of all time, and Steve Kerr, one of the best coaches in NBA history. A perfect storm led to the Pelicans' worst loss in franchise history and raised a huge red flag for the rest of the season.

The 51-point blowout was an insult to injury, as Curry did not play for much of the fourth quarter.

Golden State had over 40% of its salary cap unavailable due to devastating injuries to Jimmy Butler (recovering from an ACL tear), Moses Moody (recovering from a patellar tendon tear), and Kristaps Porziņģis (dealing with a rare disorder that threatens his NBA career). They had three players with over 25 points: Curry, Brandin Podziemski, and Yaxel Lendeborg, who is a rookie, by the way.

Even though it is just one regular-season game out of 82, this is the Pelicans' third straight loss, and it raises a massive red flag for them moving forward. The first issue is finding rotations that actually work. With a roster that has major deficiencies, including a lack of shooting and length, coach Jamahl Mosley has to figure out a way to improve the team's spacing without sacrificing rim protection, which is easier said than done.

The team has shown small glimpses of winning basketball. It all starts on the defensive end for the Pelicans by creating turnovers and limiting opponents to one shot. This mitigates, to a certain extent, the lack of shooting on the roster by leveraging most players' ability to play downhill and attack the rim.

New Orleans Pelicans forward Zion Williamson (1) reacts during the fourth quarter against the Los Angeles Clippers at Intuit Dome. Photo Credit: Kiyoshi Mio, Imagn Images via Reuters Connect

The lack of accountability from the Pelicans has haunted the team for the last 10 years. Ever since Rajon Rondo left after only one season, the Pelicans have been adrift in their search for a true locker-room leader.

The leader of a team does not need to be its superstar. Many could argue that Draymond Green fills that role for the Warriors more than Curry does. This leader needs to be vocal with both the roster and the referees.

During Anthony Davis's time in New Orleans, his personality was better suited to a secondary role than to that of a leader who holds the team accountable. That is exactly why he was so successful during his championship run with the Lakers: without a doubt, LeBron James was the leader of that team.

During the Brandon Ingram-Zion Williamson era, both players were extremely young and less vocal. Some would argue that Ingram was more of a leader, but only because Williamson missed extended periods due to injuries.

When the team traded for CJ McCollum, he brought a more professional presence to the organization. However, with the number of injuries to their core players, the team was still set up for disappointment.

Currently, the team has one veteran presence. DeAndre Jordan has taken on a leadership and mentorship role for many of the young players, including Derik Queen. His playing time is nonexistent, so having a leader who is not on the court is not 100% effective, as he cannot call out the rest of the team on the same mistakes they make season in and season out.

These mistakes include a lack of spacing on the offensive end, playing great defense for 20 seconds of the shot clock only to leave the other team's best shooter wide open, and the killer for any team: playing great defense, forcing a contested shot, only for the offense to secure second-chance points.

New Orleans Pelicans guard Jordan Poole (3) as a time out is called against the Golden State Warriors during the third quarter at Chase Center. Photo Credit: Kelley L Cox, Imagn Images via Reuters Connect

But the question remains: after an atrocious loss and a third straight defeat, what player will call out the rest of the roster?

Five-time NBA champion and Hall of Famer, the late great Kobe Bryant, became famous in the latter years of his career for calling out teammates he felt were soft, once saying that he had seen their preparation, so why would he pass them the ball? He asked the equipment guy to take away all the players' sneakers who wore Kobe's because they were "Charming soft".

The Pelicans desperately need someone willing to hold teammates accountable, because talent alone has never been enough to build a winning culture. If the results don't show any improvement by the trade window, New Orleans may hold a fire sale on most of their roster, facing a dreaded rebuild.

#2744. By the numbers: What Cooper Flagg is doing isn’t normal

After an impressive Rookie of the Year campaign in the 2025-2026 season, Cooper Flagg entered this year looking to polish his offensive game and bring the Dallas Mavericks back to relevance. So far, he's exceeded expectations in both.

Through 11 games, the Mavericks are 7-4 and have faced one of the league's tougher schedules. Flagg has played in 10 of those games and is averaging 25.9 points, 6.9 rebounds, 6.9 assists, and 2.2 steals per game. He's 19 years old. He joins a short list of only Luka Doncic and LeBron James as one of the youngest players in NBA history to average at least 25 points, 5 rebounds, and 5 assists per game. At 20 years old, Doncic averaged 28.8 points, 9.4 rebounds, and 8.8 assists per game, while James, at 20, averaged 27.2 points, 7.4 rebounds, and 7.2 assists.

What's been most impressive about his leap is Flagg's shooting. He's knocking down 50.0% of his shots, on 61.2% true shooting. He's also been excellent at the free-throw line, shooting 90.3% there. Put those numbers together, and you get a player whose scoring efficiency is looking much more advanced than you might expect from a 19-year-old. Let's take a deeper dive into the numbers.

Flagg has attempted 42 shots at the rim (in the restricted area), making 28 of them for 66.7%. That's roughly 22% of his total attempts. It's not an enormous portion of his shot diet, but he can get there whenever he wants. Flagg often uses his size and athleticism to his advantage. At 6-foot-9, he can finish with ease over smaller defenders but also has the finesse to finish around larger ones. That combination makes his drives difficult to contain. Unlike some young perimeter players who settle for difficult jumpers when their initial attack gets cut off, Flagg has multiple ways he can beat you off the dribble.

Flagg has taken 47 shots in the portion of the paint outside of the restricted area, the most of any zone on the floor. He's made 27 of them, giving him a 57.4% shooting percentage. That's roughly 26% of all his field-goal attempts. The non-restricted-area paint has become something of a sweet spot for Flagg because it allows him to use his size and touch without having to completely beat the defense to the rim. It's also a shot that can be available when a defense successfully cuts off his initial drive. His comfortability to get to this part of the floor and shoot over defenders has proven to be his bread and butter.

Nearly half of Flagg's shot attempts come inside the paint, and he's incredibly efficient, shooting 61.7% on those attempts, 55-89. A teenager being this comfortable living in the paint is pretty rare, especially in today's NBA, where outside shooting rules. Once Flagg expands his game beyond the three-point arc, he'll be unstoppable.

Flagg has Kevin Durant-like capabilities in his mid-range game. He has attempted 43 mid-range shots, second only to his 47 attempts in the non-restricted-area paint. He's made 21, good for 48.8%. That's an important number because the mid-range is often treated as something players should eliminate from their offensive diet. For Flagg, that's not necessarily the case. Use Durant as the example, who is currently fifth on the all-time NBA scoring leaders list, as he approaches 33,000 points.

At nearly 49%, Flagg is making enough of these shots to justify taking them — particularly because many of them are self-created. If a defender backs up to protect the drive, Flagg can shoot. If the defender presses up, he can attack. If the help defender steps into the lane, he can stop short. That puts a lot of pressure on the defense and leaves them with no real solution in guarding him.

There's a tendency in modern basketball analysis to look at a player's shot chart and immediately identify mid-range attempts as something that needs to be reduced. That isn't necessarily true for Flagg. An efficient mid-range shooter who can also get to the rim, shoot threes and create for teammates is a completely different proposition than a player who lives in the mid-range because he can't do anything else. Flagg is not that player. The mid-range is one part of his offensive toolkit, and right now, it's a pretty good one.

Now for the part nobody needs to sugarcoat – 29.2% from three isn't good, making 14 of 48. The shot-chart data shows that almost all of Flagg's three-point attempts are coming above the break. He has attempted 42 above-the-break threes and made only 10, good for 23.8%. That's the biggest blemish on his shooting profile. The good news is that he's actually been excellent from the corners. Flagg has attempted just six corner threes, but he's made four of them for 66.7%. Obviously, that's an extremely small sample, but worth noting. But it does reinforce an important point: the problem isn't that Flagg can't physically make a three. It's consistency, particularly on higher-volume, above-the-break attempts.

One thing not to lose in the discussion about his three-point percentage is the fact that Flagg is willing to take them. He's attempted 48 total threes. That's enough volume to matter. He's not hiding from the shot. He's not passing up every open look. He's taking the shots defenses are giving him. If he can get this percentage to 34-36%, Flagg will enter 30 points per game territory.

It's too early to call Flagg a great shooter, but at 19 he is a great scorer. Shooting wasn't his calling card coming into the NBA, but it's evolving. Being an efficient scorer in today's NBA without a reliable three-point shot (yet), bodes well for Flagg. As he continues to work on his outside shooting and that three-point percentage creeps northward, he will become one of the most unstoppable forces in the NBA. The three-point shot isn't the foundation of Cooper Flagg's offensive game. It's the potential multiplier.

Flagg arrived on the heels of Luka Doncic's departure to Los Angeles. And despite the weight of seismic expectations and a tumultuous situation when he arrived, Flagg has largely exceeded expectations. These numbers aren't normal for a teenager. They point to something much larger – the next generational superstar.

#2742. Reviewing the Bears’ PFN grades from Week 9 vs. Buccaneers

The Bears extended their winning streak to four games on Sunday night, squeezing away with a 27-24 win over the Buccaneers at home. They improved their record to 7-2 in the process, and though their offensive performance wasn't pretty, their strong defense led them to victory. As they prepare to head into their bye week in Week 10, they have a well-timed opportunity to rest up and regroup.

Each week, I'll review how Chicago's eligible performers graded by Pro Football Network's Impact Scoring model. Now that the rest of the NFL has caught up, and the numbers have all been crunched, here's how Week 9 looked.

Analytically, Caleb Williams had his worst game of the season since his Week 2 outing in the rain against the Vikings. His -0.21 EPA per dropback marked the worst average he's had in a single game all year. His four interceptions certainly played a major role in his reaching a negative average for the first time in 2026. That said, he still finished with an above-average completion percentage over expected, coming in No. 13 with a +1.0 percentage.

It's not much of a surprise that the rest of the Bears' offense didn't grade incredibly well on Sunday. The offensive interior struggled in particular, with Garrett Bradbury finishing well below average at center and Joe Thuney taking his lumps at left guard. Darnell Wright continued his stellar 2026, though, as his 89.0 PFN OL Impact grade for the year leads all offensive tackles in the NFL.

Clark Phillips III: 79.5 (21st of 101 CBs)

Tyrique Stevenson: 72.7 (63rd of 101 CBs)

Chicago's defense played a huge role in its win over the Buccaneers on Sunday, and it was highlighted by interceptions from both Jaylon Johnson and Cam Lewis. Johnson returned his interception back for a touchdown, and he allowed a flawless 0.0 passer rating when targeted in coverage in Week 9. Considering the rocky season he's had in 2026 thus far, putting together such a strong outing had to mean a lot to him. It certainly meant a lot to the Bears.

Elsewhere, the defensive standouts included Jeffery Simmons — who had another sack in his second game with the Bears — Austin Booker, and Devin Bush. Bush cleaned up with nine tackles, thriving in space as Simmons plugged up running lanes in front of him. The emergence of Clark Phillips III is a particularly interesting statistic, as he allowed a targeted passer rating of just 39.6 in coverage on Sunday.

Though Cairo Santos deserves credit for coming through in the clutch with his 38-yard field goal to win the Bears the game, the relative lack of difficulty of his kicks doesn't help his analytical profile much. His other converted field goal came from just 25 yards out, so other NFL kickers grade higher thanks to superior field goals made over expected. On the punting side of things, Tory Taylor averaged just 40.3 net yards per punt, which ranked No. 23 among 29 punters in Week 9.

#2737. Cleveland Browns 2027 mock draft: Help on defense and finally a QB

Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken finally delivered the answer on Wednesday to the question that has kept the NFL on edge since Sunday evening.

Deshaun Watson is indeed returning as the team's starting quarterback for this Sunday's game against the Houston Texans.

It was the only logical decision for Monken to make given that Watson helped the Browns to a 5-3 record before missing last week's overtime loss to the New Orleans Saints with a concussion.

Because this is Monken's first year in Cleveland, a town where manufactured quarterback debates go to thrive, he seemed genuinely puzzled on Wednesday about why he would need to make a formal announcement about the starting quarterback:

"I don't even know why I have to say it publicly, because it's really only our business in terms of who's going to play and who's not going to play. But I mean, he played well enough to earn to still be our starter."

Even though the Browns now have their starting quarterback established for the rest of this season, there are still going to be questions about what they will do in 2027.

Watson's contract is up at the end of this season, and no matter what happens the rest of the way, the Browns really need to move on from the most controversial quarterback that has ever been on the roster.

That leaves Shedeur Sanders and Dillon Gabriel, both destined for careers as backup quarterbacks, and rookie Taylen Green, whose future role in the NFL has yet to be determined.

So the Browns will need a new starting quarterback – or at least a rookie that projects to actually be a starting quarterback – which should lead general manager Andrew Berry to select one in the 2027 NFL Draft.

Berry will be holding a pair of first-round selections come draft, both Cleveland's and the one received from the Los Angeles Rams as part of the Myles Garrett trade, but neither appears as if they will be at the top of the draft.

Which means that Berry will have to either work a trade or wait and see who might fall to him on draft night.

That is the path that The Athletic's Nick Baumgardner sees Berry taking in this Round 1 mock draft, with Baumgardner projecting that the Browns will be selecting at No. 15 and No. 19 overall.

With quarterbacks Drew Mestemaker (Miami at No. 3) and CJ Carr (New York Jets at No. 6) off the board, but with (gasp!) Arch Manning still in the green room, the Browns select Clemson defensive end Will Heldt with their first pick:

Big enough, at 6-6, 260, to be an edge setter, Heldt is also crafty enough with his hands to rack up pass-rush wins. His build somewhat resembles that of Aidan Hutchinson.

Heldt is in his second season with the Tigers after playing two years at Purdue. In 46 career games so far, he has 146 tackles, 19.5 sacks, and 37.5 tackles for loss.

Four picks later at No. 19, Berry finally ends the suspense, and the Browns select quarterback Darian Mensah from Miami:

The College Football Playoff — assuming Miami gets in, as it should — figures to be a huge stretch for Mensah. The Hurricanes' star has the potential to be a top-10 pick, but he still needs to show more consistency, both downfield and as a processor when facing high-level teams. His arrow is firmly pointed up, though.

Mensah is in his first season with the Hurricanes after playing one season at Tulane (2024) and one at Duke (2025). In helping Miami to an 8-1 record, Mensah is completing 76.8 percent of his passes for 2,694 yards, 28 touchdowns, and just two interceptions.

Two first-round picks and the Browns add an impact player on defense and take their latest and greatest shot at fixing the quarterback situation.

HOUSTON - Stephen Curry was evidently none too pleased with social-media chatter around wife Ayesha Curry's first feature-film leading role in the romantic comedy "Second Chance Holiday."

A clip from the film, featuring Ayesha Curry giving an on-screen kiss to co-star Matthew Daddario, went viral this past week and served as fodder for a wide variety of podcasts. "I've been hearing a lot of noise, and usually the noise doesn't bother me, doesn't bother Ayesha, but this one in particular - when you're trying to step on the accomplishments of my wife, and obviously needing podcast tapings and topics and giving opinions on somebody else's wife - Nick, (Gilbert), Emmanuel, and anybody else who feels the need to want to have to jump in and give an opinion on something you don't really know about and kinda speaks to a bigger conversation on how you view women in this world and what they're allowed and what they're not allowed to do, even the ignorance behind how acting works," Curry said, cycling through an array of mocking faces.

#2727. Cardinals Reveal Final Decision on Carson Beck’s Week 10 Status

Beck is officially making his debut as a starting QB in the NFL. Getty

The 3-6 Arizona Cardinals are heading into a week 10 matchup against the Los Angeles Rams facing mounting issues.

Arizona is already heading into the week without WR Michael Wilson, as well as an uncertain status surrounding C Hjalte Froholdt and others.

The major conversation this week has been at quarterback, however. This comes as incumbent starter Gardner Minshew II battles through a potentially serious injury. The general expectation has been that rookie Carson Beck will take the starting reigns in week 10, but no official confirmation came before Wednesday.

GettyBeck is officially making his debut as a starting QB in the NFL.

Head coach Mike LaFleur officially announced that the rookie is starting in week 10 during a press conference. The accompanying news is that Minshew will need surgery on his elbow injury. This is unfortunate for Minshew, but it clears the way for what was inevitable regardless.

The final eight games of the Cardinals' season will seemingly serve as an audition for the Miami product. Beck, 24, was a third-round pick in April for the Cardinals. The organization – including LaFleur – clearly believes in the Florida native to a high degree.

Beck's journey to becoming the starting QB hasn't been a seamless one despite the belief. He was held out of preseason action following the first contest due to a back issue. The subsequent result was sitting behind both Jacoby Brissett and Minshew prior to week nine against the Seattle Seahawks.

Now, the stage is Beck's to prove that he is the franchise guy for the Cardinals.

The Cardinals are asking a great deal out of Beck, particularly when contextualizing the help around him.

Arizona's wide receiver core is down to Semi Fehoko, Reggie Virgil, and Devin Duvernay. Jeremiyah Love will miss at least the next three weeks during his IR stint. Bam Knight is still in concussion protocol. The offensive line is in disarray as well, with Elijah Wilkinson and Isaac Seumalo positioning to be the only players within the group to start in every game.

Beck will have megastar Trey McBride at his disposal, but there isn't much permeating outside of the all-world pass catcher.

The upcoming matchups are also daunting for Beck. Los Angeles is trotting out an elite defensive line duo in Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett. This is an immediate challenge for a rookie quarterback sitting behind a makeshift offensive line.

After this, the Cardinals travel to take on the Kansas City Chiefs. While Kansas City isn't as explosive from a pass rushing perspective, they are a relatively stingy defense overall.

The final six games will give Beck cleaner opportunities to prove himself as the future in Arizona. Upcoming matchups include porous units in the New York Jets and Las Vegas Raiders.

Until those days come, Beck will take on immediate daunting tests against challenging opponents. The Cardinals are taking on the Rams on Sunday afternoon at 2:25 P.M. MST from State Farm Stadium in Glendale.

#2725. Duke Tobin sends out 'not comfortable' head coach Zac Taylor to explain Bengals' trade-deadline snafu with Eagles

Zac Taylor almost certainly had little to nothing to do with the trade-deadline snafu on Tuesday in which the Cincinnati Bengals backed out of an agreed-upon deal with the Philadelphia Eagles.

On Wednesday, the Bengals' head coach took the podium to discuss the topic despite declaring that he was "not comfortable" doing so. He said he did it at the behest of director of player personnel and de facto general manager Duke Tobin.

Per Taylor, Tobin is "really apologetic." To be clear, that came from Taylor's mouth, not Tobin's.

"Obviously, we tried something yesterday," Taylor said. "Duke was very explicit with me when he came and spoke to me of how he wanted this portrayed. I'm not comfortable doing it, but I'm going to do what he asked.

"We did make an effort to kind of put some depth in there in place of Cashius [Howell]. As we got into it, obviously it was going to be a little more costly than we initially anticipated. He's really apologetic about it and wants to make clear: Philly was a great trade partner. It was on our end."

In case you missed it, the Bengals had an agreement with the Eagles in place to acquire edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie prior to Tuesday's trade deadline. The Bengals need depth at the position due to a wrist injury that placed Howell on injured reserve.

In the agreed upon deal, the Bengals would've sent a sixth-round pick to the Eagles and received Ebiketie in return. But it turns out the deal came at a significantly higher cost, which the Bengals' front office apparently didn't realize when it made the agreement.

Per the NFL's compensatory picks mechanisms, the Bengals would've also had to forfeit a third-round compensatory pick to acquire Ebiketie. So in essence, they would have parted with a third-round pick and a sixth-round pick to acquire a backup pass rusher.

It's a price that's prohibitive and one the Bengals reportedly didn't realize until Over the Cap's self-proclaimed "Compensatory Picks Guy™" Nick Korte pointed it out on social media.

Korte's analysis picked up traction among traditional NFL media, and only then did the Bengals back out of the deal, having realized its true cost.

This was all reported Tuesday, and Taylor was left to confirm it with media on Wednesday.

This is not Taylor's job. He's a head football coach. He's not supposed to be tasked with knowing the complex mechanics of NFL trades or the league's compensatory pick system, and he's not the one who pulled the trigger on the agreement with the Eagles.

Those responsibilities lie with the player personnel arm of Cincinnati's front office, which is run by Tobin. The mistake was an embarrassment for Tobin's department that played out across sports media on Tuesday.

On Wednesday, Tobin sent out Taylor to face the music.

#2722. Nolan Teasley: This roster has "earned the right" to maximize its potential with Kirk Cousins

On Tuesday, the Vikings worked the phones and ultimately found a new starting quarterback in Kirk Cousins. On Wednesday, the work began to get Cousins up to speed.

Although G.M. Nolan Teasley deferred to coach Kevin O’Connell as to the new depth chart with Cousins in the room, Teasley also stated the obvious in a press conference with reporters.

“We . . . didn’t acquire Kirk to not play,” Teasley said.

Teasley pointed to various factors that drew the Vikings to a reunion with Cousins, including his familiarity with the offense, the organization, and the coaching staff. Teasley also noted Cousins’s “live arm,” touch, placement, and accuracy.

Teasley also tried to push back against the perception (if not reality) that the Monday night disaster against the Bills prompted a Tuesday fire drill that ended with the trade for Cousins.

“I would tell you that it didn’t,” Teasley said regarding the impact of the Week 9 game on the outcome. “We’ve been looking for ways to improve this football team, again, for weeks. And we just followed the process. It was a wide net that we were casting. And ultimately this is what we landed on, and this was the right move for this point in time.”

Right, but it’s hard not to make the connection between Monday night’s showing and the Tuesday trade deadline. Indeed, if the trade deadline hadn’t previously been shifted from the Tuesday after Week 8 to the Tuesday after Week 9, the window may have closed before the Vikings realized how badly they needed to jump through it.

At the end of the day, it’s clear that the Vikings felt compelled to get the most out of what the team currently has.

“This roster has earned the right to explore the potential to maximize where we can take this thing,” Teasley said.

Could Cousins stay with the Vikings beyond the current season?

“There’s always potential for that, but this is really about 2026.” Teasley said. “And that’s where we’re focused. . . . When that time comes we’ll address it.”

For now, they addressed getting more out of the side of the ball that’s struggling mightily.

“We still believe in the potential of the offense,” Teasley said. “There’s a lot of really talented players over there. So this is about doing what’s best for the Vikings in totality.”

Teasley opted not to engage in a hypothetical discussion as to how Cousins impacts the team’s ceiling.

“This is a really good football team,” Teasley said. “We’re 6-2 through eight games, and we just acquired a really good football player.”

While Teasley won’t address hypotheticals, others will. Without Cousins, the Vikings were destined to implode. They wouldn’t have won enough games to make it to the playoffs.

Now? They’re in position to take the NFC North — and possibly to win a playoff game or two. If, as it appears, the trade rejuvenates the defense and elevates the offense, the Vikings will become one of the most balanced teams in the league.

Which will give them an opportunity to navigate what will be the meat grinder of the looming NFC playoff tree.

#2719. Fantasy Basketball Rankings (9-cat leagues): Early risers and fallers of the 2026-27 NBA season

We're into Week 4, and below is my 9-cat riser and faller list through Week 3, featuring five risers and five fallers. Ranks are my rest-of-season 9-cat projections, not a summary of who's performed best so far. Stats are through Nov. 9 (about 8–11 games played per player), so sample sizes are still small.

Mitchell has become one of the NBA's top playmakers. Not bad for a guy who went around pick 120 during draft season. His 8.5 assists a night rank fifth in the league, with a potential 14.8 assists per game. That's just the passing. His shot volume has almost doubled, boosting his scoring to over 16 points per game, along with 2.2 3s. And he's still getting steals, averaging over 1 per outing. The only knock to his game is his free-throw shooting. Playing high minutes on a team with little creation outside of Giannis Antetokounmpo and sometimes Pelle Larsson, Mitchell has real staying power as a PG anchor. He ranks near the top-50 in both points and 9-cat through three weeks.

It's a luxury for the Timberwolves to have a player of Ayo's caliber to step in for Anthony Edwards. He's been a model of efficiency for years and has been impactful whenever he saw an increase in minutes and opportunity. That tracks with what we've seen from Dosunmu this season. Dosunmu is shooting 52% from the field and 89% at the line, scoring 18.1 points, grabbing 4.9 rebounds, and adding 4.1 assists, while still tacking on 1.9 3s and 1.3 steals in 31 minutes. As long as Edwards is out, Ayo is a top-40 player in 9-cat and top-60 in High Score, averaging over 36 fantasy points per night.

Health is wealth. So far, Zion is pacing to last season's numbers — similar shot volume, but excelling in the paint. Zion is fourth in the league in points in the paint, averaging 14.1 per game.  Zion is shooting 63% while getting to the line 7.2 times a game. Bully ball. Also, his steal rate is pacing to a career high, with over 2 per game. That number is bound to regress, but the combination of his high FG and steal rates, improving free-throw percentage (76.4) and scoring over 20 ppg with 5 boards is what's elevated him to 22nd in 9-cat, 34th in points and 43rd in High Score. I'd sell high in each format except for High Score.

Smith is in the midst of a breakout campaign. Through 11 games, everything is clicking for the third pick of the 2022 NBA Draft. He's averaging 17.0 points, 6.5 boards, 2.7 3s, 50% shooting, 45% on 3s and 86% at the line. There's even been a boost in assists to almost 3 per game. I think it's more of a testament to Fred VanVleet's leadership and opening up the floor for the supporting cast to operate more freely. Smith's success has been one of the biggest surprises three weeks into the season. A couple more weeks of this level of play and he might be able to fetch something real on the fantasy trade market.

Bridges is definitely a riser in 9-cat leagues. He's currently 27th, averaging 15-7-3 with 45/33/87 shooting splits. He's also getting over a steal per contest. Now, while those numbers are solid, I don't trust he'll be able to keep this up all season. The supporting cast outside of Booker has been dreadful. I expect their improvements will alter some of Bridges' success to date. Bridges' rebounding numbers are pacing to the best of his career, as is his low turnover rate. But top-30 (and top 70 in High Score and points formats) is too good to be true. Sell, sell, sell.

What happened to this man? He's become Toumani Camara; 67% of Bane's shots have come from beyond the arc. He's still knocking down 3.6 a game, but he's shooting 37% overall and 36% from 3. His turnovers are up to 2.6 per contest and he's providing just 2.4 assists for a guy who went 53rd in ADP. His 15 shots per game is consistent with his past couple of seasons. The main difference is the shot diet — chucking 3s, taking half the amount of 2-point FGs and not going to the line nearly enough — a recipe for disaster and it's why he's 136th in 9-cat.

This one hurts, and the culprit is minutes. Ware is down to 17.3 a game after playing 22.2 last season, and 8.6 points and 6.9 rebounds on 40% shooting won't cut it. He's only played more than 20 minutes in two of 11 games this season. Bucks head coach Taylor Jenkins isn't giving him much leeway, similar to how Spoelstra handled him, likely because of the same mental lapses that frustrated coaches in Miami. I hyped him up, but that ADP in the high 70s always looked a bit sus considering he's still behind Myles Turner. It's a long season, but I understand if fantasy managers want to drop him.

Harden looks old. His scoring and assist numbers have fallen off a cliff — he's shooting just 36% from the field and averaging 5.7 assists (down significantly from his career averages). Turnovers are still an issue at 3.0 per game, which hurts in multiple categories, and the free-throw attempts have dropped to just 4.8 a game. There's legitimate reason to be concerned about how he's moving and producing, but I still see him as a buy-low. This feels more like an early-season slump than a full-on panic. If you can acquire him at a discount, now is the time to try.

A season ago, Rollins was a 32-minute guy averaging 17 points. Now he's playing 23 minutes and putting up 10.7 points on 38% shooting and 67% from the line and, more importantly, was passed on the depth chart by Brayden Burries. I have him 135th, but I'm giving him some grace in my latest rankings, expecting he'll turn it around somewhat — even if he's coming off the bench. He's much closer to a top-120 player than to 200, which is roughly where he sits in 9-cat through three weeks.

Six points a game on 33% shooting. That's the line, and it's ugly. Bridges put up 14.4 points on 49% shooting last season, so outside of his availability, he's giving fantasy managers nothing. I haven't found a good reason for it yet. He's playing 26 minutes a night with no offensive confidence and minimal stocks to save him on defense. I have him 134th, which is generous. Hold only if you have the bench space and the patience; otherwise, move on, especially in points leagues.
